newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Deputy Prime Minister Gen Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has threatened to abandon the government and Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa has consulted experts about his authority to dissolve the parliament. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan has announced he would pull his Nam Thai Party out of the coalition government after premier Banharn insisted that he would take responsibility for appointing finance, commerce and industry ministers in the new coalition government. (KRUNGTHEP THURAKIJ)

- Many employees of the first-class Dusit Thani Hotel have resigned following reports that the hotel would be closed down for five years during the construction of a mass transit project. A temporary station of the mass transit project is planned to be located at the hotel during the construction. (THAI THURAKIJ FINANCE)

- Economists have suggested Thai investors keep an eye on Mexico as a location for investment in supporting industries aimed at exporting products to the U.S. when the North American Free Trade Agreement comes into full affect. (THE NATION)

- The Export Promotion Department has been attacked at a meeting with major buying agents and international trading firms for allowing red tape to delay export opportunities. A company executive says the department should be blamed for a delay of export information to exporters. (BANGKOK POST)
